meta.description: Authenticates users logging into the CardDemo credit card management system and routes them to the appropriate menu based on their user type.
meta.process_description: This program presents a sign-on screen to users, collecting their User ID and Password credentials. It validates the entered credentials against a User Security file (USRSEC), checking that the user exists and that the supplied password matches the stored password. Upon successful authentication, it determines whether the user is an administrator or a regular user and routes them accordingly — administrators are directed to the Admin Menu (COADM01C) and regular users to the Main Menu (COMEN01C). If authentication fails due to a missing User ID, missing password, incorrect password, or unknown user, the sign-on screen is redisplayed with an appropriate error message.

files.USRSEC: User Security file storing registered user credentials (User ID, password, and user type) used to authenticate login attempts

business_rules: User ID is mandatory — the system will not attempt authentication if the User ID field is blank
Password is mandatory — the system will not attempt authentication if the Password field is blank
Both User ID and Password are converted to uppercase before validation, making authentication case-insensitive
A user must exist in the User Security file; if not found, access is denied with a 'User not found' message
The supplied password must exactly match the password stored in the User Security file; a mismatch results in a 'Wrong Password' error and the user must retry
Authenticated users are routed to different menus based on their user type: administrators go to the Admin Menu (COADM01C), regular users go to the Main Menu (COMEN01C)
Pressing PF3 at the sign-on screen displays a 'Thank You' message and terminates the session gracefully
Any key other than Enter or PF3 is rejected with an 'Invalid Key' error message, preventing unintended navigation

System errors during credential lookup (i.e. any response code other than 'found' or 'not found') result in an 'Unable to verify the User' message, preventing access without exposing technical details

lines.explanation: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph of the sign-on process. It determines whether a user is arriving at the screen for the first time or responding to it, then routes control based on the key pressed — presenting the sign-on screen, processing credentials, accepting a graceful exit, or rejecting invalid input — before returning control to the transaction to await the next user interaction.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group record that holds all working storage variables used during the sign-on process, including program identity, user credentials, error tracking, and messaging for the CardDemo login workflow.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this sign-on program ('COSGN00C'). Used to identify the currently executing program when passing control or logging context to other parts of the CardDemo system, ensuring the system always knows which program initiated the authentication flow.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CC00') assigned to the CardDemo sign-on transaction. This code uniquely identifies the login session in the CICS environment, ensuring that screen interactions and program re-entries are correctly associated with the sign-on process rather than any other CardDemo transaction.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed to the user on the sign-on screen. This field communicates the outcome of the login attempt — for example, 'User not found', 'Wrong Password', 'Invalid Key pressed', or 'Unable to verify the User' — guiding the user on what went wrong and what action to take next.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The name of the User Security file ('USRSEC') that stores registered user credentials. This value is used to reference the correct file when looking up a user's stored User ID, password, and user type during the authentication process.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An internal flag that tracks whether a validation error has occurred during the sign-on process. It starts as 'N' (no error) and is set to 'Y' if any business rule is violated (e.g., blank User ID, wrong password, user not found), preventing the system from proceeding with authentication when an error condition exists.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: A named condition that is true when a sign-on validation error has been detected (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'). When this condition is active, the system knows it must stop the authentication flow, display an appropriate error message, and prompt the user to correct their input.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: A named condition that is true when no sign-on validation error has been detected (WS-ERR-FLG = 'N'). When this condition is active, the system knows the login process is proceeding cleanly and can continue to the next validation step or grant access.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The response code returned by CICS after attempting to read the User Security file. This code tells the system whether the file read succeeded, whether the user record was not found, or whether a system-level error occurred — directly driving the business decision of whether to authenticate, reject, or display a system error to the user.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The reason code returned by CICS alongside the response code after the User Security file lookup. It provides additional technical detail about why a file operation succeeded or failed, supporting error diagnosis when the system cannot verify user credentials and must display a generic 'Unable to verify the User' message.

variables.name: WS-USER-ID
variables.description: The User ID entered by the person attempting to log in, captured from the sign-on screen. After being converted to uppercase, this value is used as the key to look up the user's record in the User Security file. If this field is blank, the system immediately rejects the login attempt without querying the file.

variables.name: WS-USER-PWD
variables.description: The password entered by the person attempting to log in, captured from the sign-on screen. After being converted to uppercase, this value is compared against the password stored in the User Security file for the given User ID. A mismatch results in a 'Wrong Password' error, and the user must retry. If this field is blank, the login attempt is rejected immediately.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area passed between transactions and programs. In the sign-on context, this area carries session and user information (such as authenticated user type and ID) from the sign-on program to downstream CardDemo programs, enabling role-based routing to either the Admin Menu or the Main Menu after successful login.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: A minimal placeholder within the CICS communication area, used to detect whether the sign-on program is being entered for the first time (no prior commarea) or re-entered after a screen interaction. Its presence or absence tells the program whether to display a fresh sign-on screen or to process credentials that the user has just submitted.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph of the sign-on process. It determines whether a user is arriving at the screen for the first time or responding to it, then routes control based on the key pressed — presenting the sign-on screen, processing credentials, accepting a graceful exit, or rejecting invalid input — before returning control to the transaction to await the next user interaction.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the user's login submission by collecting and validating the credentials entered on the sign-on screen. It enforces mandatory field rules, normalises the credentials to uppercase for case-insensitive comparison, and triggers the lookup of the user's record in the security file if all basic validations pass.

paragraphs.name: SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Prepares and displays the sign-on screen to the user, including any error or informational message resulting from a failed or initial authentication attempt. This paragraph is the final step in presenting the login interface, ensuring the user sees current feedback before re-entering credentials.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.description: Displays a plain-text message to the user on the terminal screen and immediately ends the session transaction. This is used to communicate a final status or error message — such as a graceful sign-off acknowledgement — before returning control to the CICS environment.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Assembles the standard header information displayed at the top of the sign-on screen, including application titles, the current date and time, and system identifiers, so that users see a consistent and accurately timestamped interface when they attempt to log in.

paragraphs.name: READ-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs the core authentication check by looking up the user's credentials in the User Security file and, upon successful verification, routes the authenticated user to the appropriate menu based on their role. If authentication fails for any reason, it redisplays the sign-on screen with a specific error message guiding the user on how to proceed.
